$comment: The source of sf-modal's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/modal (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

modal-id.summary: The window's id: data-sf-modal-close and data-sf-modal-hide controls name it. Empty: the element's id, else a path id.

heading.summary: The window's title in the default header. Empty: the text of the page's language ("Dialog" in English).

text.summary: Plain text in the body when no content is given.

autoload.summary: Opens the window once, without animation, as soon as it is drawn.

minimizable.summary: Shows a minimize button in the header (not in inline display); minimize() and the minimized attribute keep the window open but out of view.

overlay.summary: Draws the scrim behind the window (never in inline display).

show-header.summary: Draws the header: the heading (or the header slot) and its buttons.

show-close.summary: Draws the close button in the header, while the window is dismissible.

close-on-esc.summary: Escape closes the top window, while it is dismissible.

close-on-overlay.summary: A press on the scrim closes the top window, while it is dismissible.

initial-focus.summary: Where the focus goes when the window opens (decisions C25, C39): auto -- the page's [autofocus], else in a question window (one holding a dangerous answer or an sf-confirm) its safe answer «Отмена», else the panel; safe -- the safe answer whenever there is one; first -- the first control of its content (the header's × excluded); panel -- the panel.

preserve-scroll-gap.summary: While the page is locked, adds the scrollbar's width to the page's end padding so the content does not shift; false leaves the padding alone.

position.summary: Where the window stands: center, a side panel at inline-start or inline-end (following the document direction), top or bottom; left and right are the physical forms.

size.summary: The window's kind of size (decision C39). auto: as wide as its content or width says. question: a question window -- --sf-popup-question-width (28rem, compact 26rem), the frame --sf-space-3, the title at text step 2 in bold, the title, the content and the footer on one start line, the × on the padding's corner, the footer's answers at the start and --sf-space-3 after the content; on a phone (below sm, 32rem) a window left at the centre opens as a bottom sheet. width, when given, still wins.

mode.summary: Where the content comes from: inline (the element's own content), ajax (fetched from src: a URL, or #id whose content is taken) or iframe (src in a frame).

display.summary: modal: a dialog over the page; inline: a region in the page's flow, shown without open.

src.summary: For mode ajax, a URL to fetch or #id of an element whose content is taken; for mode iframe, the frame's URL.

preload.summary: Loads src before the window opens; false loads it at the first opening.

fullscreen.summary: The window takes the whole viewport.

width.summary: The panel's width, a CSS length (sets --sf-modal-width).

height.summary: The panel's height, a CSS length (sets --sf-modal-height).

backdrop-blur.summary: Blurs the page behind the scrim: present or true for the blur-type strength, or a strength itself (none, small, medium, large).

overlay-preset.summary: The scrim: default, the shared black 64 scrim; focus, the same with a small backdrop blur.

overlay-class.summary: Classes on the scrim; applied last, so they win over the preset.

surface-padding.summary: The surface's padding, a CSS length (sets --sf-modal-surface-padding).

panel-class.summary: Classes on the panel, the box that holds the surface.

body-class.summary: Classes on the body's scrolling area.

content-class.summary: Classes on the wrapper of the slotted content.

footer-class.summary: Classes on the footer. Its actions stand at the end with --sf-modal-footer-gap (space-1/2) between them; those defaults sit under the utilities, so a utility here still wins.

unsaved.summary: Something in the window is unsaved: the close request (sf-modal-close) carries it as detail.unsaved, so a page can ask before it lets the window close.

dismissible.summary: false: Escape, a press on the scrim and the close button no longer close the window; close() and the page's own controls still do.

open.x-answer: asked by an assembly (ask, §19.4) it answers when the window closes, with value {accepted, reason, value}
open.summary: Opens the window, or brings it to the front when already open. Dispatches sf-modal-open (cancelable), then sf-modal-opened once projected; loads remote content when src is set. options.animate (or a boolean) controls the opening transition. Returns the element.

close.summary: Closes the window after sf-modal-close (cancelable), runs the close transition, restores focus and dispatches sf-modal-closed. options.reason says why (close, escape, outside, cancelled, api; api by default) and is carried by both events. Returns the element.

toggle.summary: Calls close() when open, open() otherwise. Returns the element.

reload-content.summary: Resets the remote content and loads src again, even when the window is closed and preload is off. Returns the element.

confirm.x-summary: Closes the window as the person's acceptance: the answer of ask is {accepted: true, reason: close, value} (§19.4)

relations.name: cl-button-close
$comment: The close button: sf-button-close (owner decision C14).

relations.name: spinner
$comment: spinner: the remote content's loading state shows it, fetched after the page is ready.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16): the build does not compile template.html yet, so a second copy of the markup would only drift from the one that draws.

--sf-modal-question-width.x-summary: The width of a question window (size="question"); --sf-popup-question-width by default: 28rem, 26rem in a compact region.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-modal for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split (the old detail from the element's adapter), attribute-and-property, host-attribute (no shim), inverted (read by the component), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

rows.summary: Dated alias of heading until 2026-12-01: the window's title.

rows.note: blur is a method of HTMLElement and the base action; the attribute is mapped, the property stays the browser's
the attribute only: the property name hide is the old method, an action alias of minimize
inverted: unclose present means dismissible false; the shim maps values one to one, so it refuses this row (mode-on-non-event) and sf-modal reads the attribute itself, noting it with these dates
stays a host attribute, read by the base (§3.1, §4.8); no shim
the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired before the window opens; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired after the window opens. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired before the window closes; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired after the window closes. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired before the window is minimized; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired after the window is minimized. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired before the window is shown again after being minimized; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Fired after the window is shown again after being minimized. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: An Ajax content request (mode=ajax) is starting. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: the old detail adds component, modal and root (page elements, which §8 takes out of the new detail): the element's detail adapter makes it
rows.summary: Remote content finished loading, with success or error in detail.remote; an aborted request does not emit it. Also fired when an iframe loads. Bubbles and is composed.

rows.note: a reader retires; the method stays until the date and notes each call
a reader retires; slots are placed, never copied; the method stays until the date and notes each call
a lifecycle copy; sf-after-render is the base's; still sent until the date, noted when a listener reads it
rows.summary: The window rendered for the first time. Bubbles and is composed; detail.modal is the emitting sf-modal.

rows.note: a lifecycle copy; sf-after-render is the base's; still sent until the date, noted when a listener reads it
rows.summary: The window rendered again after its first render. Bubbles and is composed; detail.modal is the emitting sf-modal.

x-summary: A dialog window over the page in the shared modal stack: centered or at a side, top or bottom edge, with header, content and footer slots, focus trap, scroll lock and focus return. It can also be minimized, load its content by Ajax or into an iframe, or render inline in the page flow.
x-renamed: settings.title → heading: "title" is a property of HTMLElement.prototype (§3.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
settings.blur → backdrop-blur: "blur" is a method of HTMLElement.prototype and the base action (§3.1, §4.1, §16 item 26), alias dated
settings.hide → minimizable: one name meant a setting (show the minimize button) and an action (minimize); the attribute is a dated alias
settings.unclose → dismissible (inverted): §19.3; the attribute is read until 2026-12-01
settings.aria-label: a host attribute, read by the base, never a setting (§3.1)
settings.minimized → values.minimized: a person changes it (the minimize button), §4
actions.hide → minimize, actions.show → expand: vocabulary §5 minimize; dated action aliases
events modal:ready, modal:update retire (§4.1, §16.13); readers getModalRoot, getSlotHtml retire (§4.4, §16.13)
x-decisions: own-verb-words: minimize is a verb of vocabulary §5 (modal `hide`), so minimize/minimized are not own verbs; content-upload and content-uploaded stay own verbs with their words in lang events.<verb>.label (§8, vocabulary §5.1).

alias-conflict: vocabulary 1.1.5 decides. modal:after-hide → sf-modal-minimized and modal:after-show → sf-modal-expanded (the facts of minimize and expand, vocabulary §4; `change` reports a person's value change only, §8), modal:before-show → sf-modal-expand (the table's sf-modal-minimize is the reverse act), the content events → sf-modal-content-upload(ed) (loading is not a value change). The converter's sf-modal-hidden/-shown/-hide/-show never shipped and get no rows.

detail-adapter: §8 takes page elements out of detail, so the new names carry {modalId, phase, …} only; each old modal:* name keeps its old detail (component, modal, root added) through a split row and the element's detail adapter (sfAliasAdapters), sent after the new name with one shared cancel.
version: 1.3.0 → 1.4.0, a minor while the renamed members hold dated aliases (§4.10); the major comes with the sweep after 2026-12-01.

existing-aliases: compatibility.migrations lists no alias; its note (events bubble, detail.modal names the emitter) is kept by the old names' adapters. The undated page triggers data-sf-modal-open/close/show/hide stay as aliases of data-sf-action (§16.10).
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows; no template.html until the build compiles one.

examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json and studio.scenario.json (the default window, an unclosable one, a minimizable one, a side panel); probe.json drives Tab, Shift+Tab and Escape (gate 16).
css-variables: the eight public variables the sheet already reads (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json); the portal carries their computed values from the host (§19.1).
side-effects: the window draws at the end of body or of its [data-sf-overlay-container] (portal), locks the page (locks-page, one lease of the layer stack) and fetches src in mode ajax (network).
layer: kind modal, locks-page, traps-focus (§19.1, §19.2); Escape, an outside press and Tab reach it only while it is the top layer.

dismissing: the close request carries {reason, unsaved} (§19.3): close (its own button), escape, outside (the overlay), cancelled (a page control, data-sf-modal-close), api (a script); unsaved is the setting unsaved; dismissible=false (alias unclose) removes escape and outside, never an explicit action.

asking a person (§19.4): open asked by an assembly (a call with a signal) answers when the window closes with value {accepted, reason, value}; accepted is true only through the action confirm (data-sf-action="<id>.confirm"). A page's own call answers at once.
instance ids (§7.1.1, simai/ui-source#41): a window without modal-id or id takes its path id (sf-modal-<n> in document order, not a module counter); the title id is <path>--title.
accessibility.name: aria-label on the host wins, else the heading (aria-labelledby the title, or aria-label when the header is a slot).

version 1.4.1: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.
version 1.4.6: the outcomes applied and refused come from core/js/element-manifest.js (core.runtime 1.25.0, duplication audit A-26) instead of a copy of its own; behaviour unchanged.

version 1.5.6: the elevated window is the modal place (C20, the shadow system, owner 2026-11-08): --sf-shadow-modal on --sf-surface-popup, over the shared scrim, black 64 (it was black at 60); the overlay-preset summary says so. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: the portal at the end of the body carries the variables of the area the element stands in -- every custom property whose value at the host differs from the portal's own, except the window's --sf-modal-* names -- so a block's retuned roles and its parts' public variables reach the window and its content. The public --sf-modal-* variables still travel by name; the private ones never do, so a window opened from another keeps its own sizes. The carrying is core's (carryLayerOrigin area/except, core.runtime 1.43.0), shared with sf-drawer 1.9.0. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives each action's method its one object argument, open({animate}), close({reason}), confirm({value}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object); the element's code also takes the value alone, open(<boolean>), and the reference says so (x-registry.action-calls). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: the window drawn in its portal stands in the density of the place the modal is in, and the sizes its template gives are relative to it (density, decision C22): a window opened from a compact region is compact; the page content it holds keeps its own explicit sizes. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The close action's reason is optional, as the element reads it (close() closes with reason api), so the reference no longer calls close's argument required. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a window inserted with open already set gives focus back to the element that inserted it (fix/drawer-focus-added-open, probe layer-added-open-focus). Also: a minor (decision C25). The window's first focus is the element the page marked with the standard autofocus attribute inside it, as a native <dialog> does -- for a dangerous question, the safe answer («Отмена»), so a stray Enter or Space only closes the window; a marked element that is not focusable itself (sf-button, display: contents) hands the focus to its first tab stop. Without a mark, or when the marked element cannot take the focus, the panel takes it, as before. One helper for the class and the Smart window (component/modal/js/_focus.js focusModalInitial, component.modal 1.1.0). Settings, events and actions unchanged.

version 1.6.0 (2026-11-10): initial-focus (decisions C25, C39; DEV's call on the ui-doc «Рецепты» gaps). auto, the default: the page's [autofocus], else in a question window -- one holding a dangerous answer (status="danger") or an sf-confirm -- its safe answer («Отмена»: the sf-confirm's declining answer, or the page's [data-sf-modal-close] answer, the header's × excluded), else the panel as before; safe, first and panel name the target outright. An answer or a marked element drawn after the window opened (an sf-button or sf-confirm still loading) is waited for, frame by frame up to two seconds, while the focus is still on the panel. The shared rule is component.modal's (_focus.js, 1.2.0), so ordinary Modal follows it too. A delete window needs no autofocus for its «Отмена» now. tests/browser/modal-initial-focus.browser.mjs.

version 1.6.1 (2026-11-10): a patch (recipes gaps acceptance D3, D4; component.modal 1.2.1). Only the answers make a question window: an sf-button with status="danger" (or its dated alias error), a drawn .sf-button--danger, or an sf-confirm. A red sf-badge or any other status="danger" in the body no longer sends the first focus to «Закрыть», where a stray Enter closed the window. Escape on an sf-confirm in the window closes the window with the decline (sf-confirm 1.1.2), so a host that sets no outcome is not left with greyed answers. Settings, values and events unchanged; tests/browser/modal-initial-focus.browser.mjs.

version 1.7.0 (2026-11-10): a minor (decision C39, the owner's yes 2026-11-09; ui-control control/research/2026-11-09-modal-look.md, round 2, option 1). size="question": the danger question window. Its width is the core token --sf-popup-question-width (28rem; 26rem in a compact region, C32's rule; core.runtime 1.53.0), read through the new public --sf-modal-question-width; its frame is --sf-space-3 (24 / compact 20 / phone 16); the default title is text step 2 in bold (sf-modal-title, not title-3); the body's 1/4 scroll inset (kept for the focus rings) is taken out of the frame, so the title, the content and the footer start on one line; the title is --sf-space-1 above the content; the × stands on the frame's corner; a footer's answers stand at the start, --sf-space-3 below the content. Below sm (32rem) a question window left at the centre opens as a bottom sheet. Every bottom window now rounds only its top corners and draws no bottom edge, and one whose frame is the window's own keeps the home-indicator area clear (env(safe-area-inset-bottom)). Reopening a window puts its question again: an sf-confirm in it that took the decline with no outcome from the host (Escape, «Отмена») is opened afresh, so its answers are live (component.modal 1.3.0; sf-confirm 1.3.0 answeredNo). «Отмена» of a window-form sf-confirm closes the window (reason cancelled) once the decline has gone through the page; a host that cancels sf-confirm-answer keeps the window. No colour, shadow or icon changes. tests/browser/modal-question-window.browser.mjs. Also (C39 acceptance D1, before release): a window closed while its own question (sf-confirm appearance="window") is still put -- by the ×, the backdrop, Escape on the window or the host's close() -- reports the decline (sf-confirm-answer {accepted: false}), as «Отмена» does, and every opening and closing clears the typed name (sf-confirm clearRequire). tests/browser/confirm-window-close.browser.mjs.

version 1.7.0 also (2026-11-10, dispatcher decision after the docs pre-check, through component.modal 1.3.0): every window takes the question window's frame and title (C39), not only size="question". The frame is --sf-space-3 (24 on a desktop, 16 on a phone; was --sf-space-2, 20 / 16), the stated default of --sf-modal-padding-block and --sf-modal-padding-inline; the title is sf-modal-title, text step 2 in bold (20 / 16; was title-3, 24 / 18), centred on the close button's line; no line under the header, as before. A page's padding, surface-padding and its own header still win. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.0, also (2026-11-11, owner decision C44 with the C39 question window; written as 1.5.7 on fix/c44-headings-density): a window's title is sf-modal-title at the heading-3 step (24 on the desktop), and a question window's keeps C21's heading-4 step in bold (20 on 28); neither moves in a compact region, on <html> or on a container. This replaces the 2026-11-10 line above for windows that are not questions: their title is no longer text step 2. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.7.0 also (2026-11-11, DEV navigation acceptance D1, through component.modal 1.3.0): one start line in every window (C39). The body scrolls inside a 1/4 inset that keeps the focus rings whole; that inset stood the content 1/4 right of the title. The scroll box now stands out into the frame by the same 1/4, so the title, the content and the footer answers start on the frame's line (24 / 16), and the rings still fit. A question window keeps its own arrangement (the inset taken out of the frame); a page's surface-padding keeps its body where it put it. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: loose content goes through the base's slot hold (holdSlotNode), as slotted content does; sf-modal does not hold its children, so nothing changes. Also: a slotted child the base still holds is not taken a second time as loose content. Also (DEV acceptance 2026-11-11, N2): the window drawn in its portal stays out of view (the style gate, data-sf-style-pending) until the sheets it draws with are applied, at most styleReadyTimeout; under held-back sheets an open window painted for a moment as a card in the page flow. A window that opened meanwhile takes its first focus once it shows. Also (N3): the first-paint sheet list no longer names utility/title (the title is sf-modal-title since C39).

version 1.7.0 also (2026-11-11, modal follow-ups, items a and b): the page's children stay in the document until the window draws. Slotted and loose, they were taken out when the window connected and placed when it drew, one or more tasks later; a page that looked its sf-menu up by id once sf-modal was defined found nothing on 20 of 20 loads. The window now holds them (static holdsSlotNodesUntilDrawn, smart-base holdSlotNode) and its drawing takes them out and places them in the same task (releaseHeldSlotNodes before the drawing). And a closed window's content starts while it is closed: the Loader leaves a Smart element inside the closed (inert) root until it opens, so a page that waited for customElements.whenDefined('sf-menu') before opening the window waited for ever. Once the page has loaded and the browser is idle, the window asks for the tags in it (SF.Loader.ensure, core layer-stack startClosedLayerContent), and they draw inside the closed root, which shows nothing; a closed container inside the window keeps its own deferral. The portal's style gate moved to the base (holdPortalUntilStyled). Settings, values, events, keys and the drawing unchanged; tests/browser/layer-closed-content.browser.mjs. The early start starts the content's code, not its data: a component that fetches its own data (sf-include) waits for the window to open, and content the page adds to the closed layer later starts the same way (the layer watches its closed root). It costs a page that never opens the window the code and sheets its content needs, fetched after the load event when the browser is idle (about 515 KB uncompressed for an sf-menu). SF_BOOT_CONFIG.startClosedLayerContent = false keeps the old timing (ui-control evidence 2026-11-11-modal-followups-2-accept, M1, M2, L1, L2).

version 1.7.1 (2026-11-13): a patch, through component.modal 1.3.1, after 1.7.0 was released (written as "1.7.0 also" on fix/modal-lows and fix/modal-title-line). The pair next 2 follow-ups (2026-11-11, DEV's acceptance L1, L2; owner decision C56, variant B): a side panel (left, right, inline-start, inline-end) stands flush to its edge of the screen as the bottom sheet does -- square corners and no border on the screen's edge, top and bottom, the inner corners keep the window's radius and the inner side its border, and on a phone (below md) the panel is the whole screen with no radius and no border; the body's outset into the frame is never more than --sf-modal-padding-inline, so a page's frame below 1/4 keeps the scroll box inside the window; the window's portal waits for its sheets themselves (at most portalStyleTimeout, 15 s), not the host gate's 3 s. And (dispatcher, 2026-11-11): a question window's title stands on the h4 step's own line, --sf-heading-4--height (20 on 24 on a desktop, 16 on 18 on a phone); it was --sf-title--height-6, 40 on a desktop and 28 on a phone, a step of the title ladder, so the header stood 16 px taller than its title. And (owner decision C79, 2026-11-12, through core/js/layer-stack.js): a window with an explicit size opened from a compact region (data-sf-density="compact") now carries that density to its portal and comes down one ladder step, as a window without a size does; it took the normal ladder before, because the size attribute on the host answered "normal". data-sf-density="normal" on the host or a region around it keeps the normal steps. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.8.0 (2026-11-14, drawer study DR-2 and modal study MD-1, MD-2, MD-3; dispatcher ruling): a minor. The header's close is sf-button-close (owner decision C14), at the 1/3 step as before; its button keeps the classes sf-modal-header-action and sf-modal-close-button (and close-class), its host (class sf-modal-close) data-sf-modal-close; the rule loads cl-button-close, and the question window's safe answer never counts that host. With component.modal 1.3.4: a window is never taller than the screen -- the header and the footer stay, the body scrolls (a 40-paragraph window stood 2588 px at a 900 px screen, its title and answers off screen); the footer's actions are a button group's gap apart, --sf-space-1/3 (8, compact 4; C144). Before its code a closed window's content stands out of the page flow (core.styles placeholder rule; inline windows keep their box). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged; the footer's order and alignment are unchanged.

version 1.7.2 (2026-11-13, owner decision C105, role H6; spacing audit D1, through component.modal 1.3.2): a patch. Every window's frame, the question window's included, is --sf-space-2 with the window's 1 px edge counted inside it: the title, the content and the answers start 20 from the outer edge on a desktop and 16 in compact density and on a phone. It was --sf-space-3 outside the edge (25 / 21 / 17), from the docs pre-check of 2026-11-10, which C105 (2026-11-12: «24 was a slip of the record») supersedes (dispatcher ruling). A side a window draws no edge on -- a side panel's screen edge, top and bottom, every side of a side panel on a phone, a bottom sheet's bottom -- takes the whole --sf-space-2. --sf-modal-padding-block and --sf-modal-padding-inline, when a page sets them, are the padding itself; surface-padding still wins. The body's outset into the frame reads the same frame. The class window (component.modal's own surface, new Modal(...)) takes the same frame: its p-3 utility gave way to a rule in sf.base, so a padding utility in surfaceClass still wins. A question window opened as a bottom sheet keeps the whole step below its answers (no bottom edge). Markup, first-paint snapshots, settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-modal for one bounded task that temporarily owns the top interaction layer. It shares stack, focus return and scroll-lock ownership with ordinary Modal. Prefer center or logical inline-start/inline-end/top/bottom positions; left/right are compatibility aliases. The dialog and iframe are large surfaces on --sf-radius--surface, while compact header actions retain --sf-radius--ui. Inline display stays in document flow and does not capture focus. Minimized instances remain open but leave the visible interaction stack.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not use Modal for a long independent workflow that belongs on its own page
Do not replace semantic spacing, motion, color or radius tokens with absolute design values
Do not assume remote or iframe content is trusted; the host owns CSP, permissions, errors and data decisions
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

accessibility.focus: Opening focuses, by initial-focus, the page's [autofocus], else the safe answer of a question window («Отмена»), else the panel of the top window; Tab and Shift+Tab are trapped inside it and Escape closes it when close-on-esc allows. Closing returns focus to the opener. The default title names the dialog through aria-labelledby; supply aria-label for a custom or headerless header. display=inline keeps normal document navigation. With display=inline the window is a region in the page rather than a dialog.

changes: modal:* events bubble and are composed, like the base modal component and sf-drawer; detail.modal names the emitting modal.
onBeforeOpen, onAfterOpen and the other on* helpers, and handlers passed to SF.create, still receive only that modal's own events.
Ancestor listeners added with addEventListener now also see events of nested modals; check event.detail.modal.

modal:after-close.summary: Fired after the window closes. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-closed's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

reason.description: Why it closes (standard 1.3.8 §19.3): its own close control, Escape, a press outside, a page control that closes it, or a script.

modal:after-hide.summary: Fired after the window is minimized. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-minimized's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:after-open.summary: Fired after the window opens. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-opened's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:after-show.summary: Fired after the window is shown again after being minimized. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-expanded's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:before-close.summary: Fired before the window closes; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-close's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

reason.description: Why it closes (standard 1.3.8 §19.3): its own close control, Escape, a press outside, a page control that closes it, or a script.

unsaved.description: Whether something is unsaved; false until the component has an unsaved setting.

modal:before-hide.summary: Fired before the window is minimized; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-minimize's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:before-open.summary: Fired before the window opens; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-open's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:before-show.summary: Fired before the window is shown again after being minimized; cancelable -- preventDefault() keeps it as it is. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-expand's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:ready.summary: The window rendered for the first time. Bubbles and is composed; detail.modal is the emitting sf-modal.

modal:update.summary: The window rendered again after its first render. Bubbles and is composed; detail.modal is the emitting sf-modal.

modal:before-content-upload.summary: An Ajax content request (mode=ajax) is starting. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-content-upload's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

modal:after-content-upload.summary: Remote content finished loading, with success or error in detail.remote; an aborted request does not emit it. Also fired when an iframe loads. Bubbles and is composed. Its detail is sf-modal-content-uploaded's with component, modal (the element) and root (its rendered root) added.

getSlotHtml.summary: Returns the HTML of the captured content for a named slot, for reading. The window does not draw from it: it places the page's own nodes (standard 1.3.8 §4.5).

hide.summary: Minimizes an open overlay window after sf-modal-minimize (cancelable) and dispatches sf-modal-minimized. Does nothing inline. Returns the element.

show.summary: Restores a minimized window after sf-modal-expand (cancelable) and dispatches sf-modal-expanded. Returns the element.

setSrc.summary: Sets the src attribute, aborts and resets the current remote content and loads the new source when it may load now. Returns the element.

getModalRoot.summary: Returns the rendered .sf-modal element, or null before render.

onKeyDown.summary: The document keydown handler the modal binds itself: Escape closes the top open window when close-on-esc allows it, Tab is trapped inside it. Not meant to be called by a host.

resetRemoteContent.summary: Clears the loaded remote HTML, error and loading state and aborts a running request.

clearPortal.summary: Unrenders and removes the portal root the window was projected into, if any.

onBeforeOpen.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-open on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onAfterOpen.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-opened on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onBeforeClose.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-close on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onAfterClose.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-closed on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onBeforeHide.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-minimize on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onAfterHide.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-minimized on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onBeforeShow.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-expand on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onAfterShow.summary: Adds a listener for sf-modal-expanded on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.

onModalReady.summary: Calls the handler at once with a modal:ready event when the modal has already rendered, otherwise adds a listener for its own modal:ready. Returns the element.

onModalUpdate.summary: Adds a listener for modal:update on the host that runs only for this modal's own events. Returns the element.
